steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Lightly grease two 9x5-inch loaf pans.
Stir milk, lemon juice, and vanilla together in a small bowl; let stand for 10 minutes.
Mix 1 ½ cups brown sugar, oil, and egg in a large bowl. Combine flour, salt, and baking soda; stir into sugar mixture alternately with milk mixture just until combined. Fold in rhubarb and walnuts.
Pour batter into prepared loaf pans. Combine remaining 1/4 cup brown sugar, butter, and cinnamon in a small bowl. Sprinkle this mixture over the unbaked loaves.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center of a loaf comes out clean, about 40 to 60 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Rhubarb Bread
raw_recipe.description: Rhubarb bread is a delicious, fruity, tangy treat. This recipe makes two tasty loaves bursting with rhubarb pieces and walnuts for a springtime treat.
raw_recipe.name: Rhubarb Bread

review.reviewBody: Great recipe! I made the healthier version described by another reviewer and substituted half the oil for an equal amount of applesauce. I also substituted 1/4 cup whole wheat flour for 1/4 cup of the white flour. It turns out a loaf that is not too sweet but has a nice tart-sweet taste. I devoured one loaf in just a day by myself. Next time I will try all applesauce for the oil and more whole wheat flour for the white flour.

Such a great way to use rhubarb other than in pie! I did make some changes based on others’ notes: 1. Reduced milk to 3/4 C. 2. Reduced oil to 1/2 C. 3. Added a heaping teaspoon. of cinnamon to dry ingredients. 4. Increased rhubarb to 3 C. To bake this, I put a scant 1/3 cup of batter in each square of a square muffin pan, then poured the remaining batter in a loaf pan (filled it about half way). The muffins were done at 25 minutes and the loaf was done at 40 minutes. This is such a moist bread/cake/muffin! Great with strawberry jam!! 🥰

Not bad, recipe is a keeper! I did not add nuts & I added WAY more rhubarb because I actually like to taste it in my breads and it adds a little bit more moisture. I had a mix of small/lg pieces of rhubarb and used at least 6 cups of it. I used mini loaf pans and finally tried my muffin top pan that I've had for yrs. Muffin tops I filled about half way and baked for about 20min? I may try less next time..and add even more rhubarb to them to make them more moist than cake like. Mini loaf so far tasted great!! I didn't make the drizzle for the top...with all the loaves/muffins I would have needed to make more than the recipe called and said forget about it! Instead, to try it out, I just sprinkled some brown sugar on top the mixture before baking and tried to pat it down a tad.

The 5 star rating is for the flavor and delicious moistness of the bread. I have made two batches now, and a couple things were problematic. 1) at 325 degrees I had to cook the loaves for an hour, and 2) getting the bread out of the pans didn't work well at all with just oiling. The second time I floured the pans as well and it worked much better. Also, I allergic to walnuts, and it was super yummy with just rhubarb. The second time I added chocolate chips!

High Altitude Adjustments: This recipe turned out great; nice & moist. I live at 5000 ft elevation so all my baking needs adjustment. I made the following changes to this recipe: less 2 TBSP sugar; decrease baking soda to 3/4 tsp; add 2 TBSP flour; add 2 TBSP milk. Increase baking temp to 350 degrees and it required 55 min of baking time. I used frozen rhubarb so I used a 2 cup package and drained most of the excess liquid. I gave it for Christmas gift to a rhubarb lover and they really liked it too. Happy baking!

Made a couple times now. Love the bites with rhubarb pieces. The first time with apple sauce replacing all the oil; the bread turned out yummy but too sweet and too soft. The next time was oil and lots of big rhubarb, 3/4c sugar, plus extra flour to boost the density since I wanted it more Bread-like. Great result and gave to neighbors also.

Husband and discriminating grandson (considers himself a foodie) gave it a two-thumbs up! I tweaked the recipe a bit. I chopped the rhubarb into 1/4" pieces and patted dry with a paper towel to remove excess moisture. Also increased rhubarb to 1-3/4 cup. Additionally, sifted the dry ingredients together along with a 1/2 tsp. cinnamon. Used half applesauce and half oil as others have suggested. I made a streusel topping containing 1/4 cup packed brown sugar, 3 tablespoons flour, 2 tablespoons oatmeal, 1/2 tsp. cinnamon and cut 2 tablespoons of softened butter which I sprinkled across top of loaves. Baked in three 8" x 3" pans.

I replaced 1/2 c. Wheat flour for white, 1/2 tsp. Cinnamon in batter and 1/4 tsp. Cinnamon in topping, 3 cups of rhubarb, mixed in 2 Tbsp. of quick oats with topping ingredients and no walnuts. I baked them in 8x4 pans but next time will use 9x4 as that much rhubarb made them quite full!! It is delicious and very moist.
great recipe but tweaked it a bit. I did 1/2 oil and 1/ 2 apple sauce, added 1/2 teaspoon of salt and 1 teaspoon of baking powder, doubled the topping and baked it for 55 minutes

This turned out SO well! Just wanted to let folks know, this recipe veganizes very easily and comes out pretty great. I made some substitutions based on preference and some just because I was missing ingredients (like I used white vinegar in place of lemon juice because I was out of lemon juice). I replaced half a cup of white flour w/ coconut flour (then added in an extra half cup of liquid so it didn't dry out). I used vanilla almond milk in place of regular milk, replaced half the oil with applesauce (as per other commenters), used a flax "egg" (1 Tbsp flax meal, 3 Tbsp water), added an extra half cup rhubarb (per another suggestion), used nearly a full tsp of cinnamon both in the batter AND in the topping, and anywhere it says oil or butter, used coconut oil. I did have to bake it a bit longer, but that often happens when I sub in coconut flour (and thus need extra liquid). SO GOOD. I was worried the sugar might be a bit high, but this bread is not too sweet at all, just enough to balance to tartness of the rhubarb. Definitely give it a try!

Tasty and simple. Per some suggestions of other reviewers, I 1) reduced the oil to just over 1/2 a cup (but did not replace the difference with applesauce due to not having any on hand, but it was perfectly moist and not oily at all using just the amount I used), 2) used about 2 1/2 cups of rhubarb, 3) poured about 2/3 of the batter into a bread dish and used the remainder to make 6 muffins, 4) I omitted the crumb topping altogether to save a few calories and found that it was definitely sweet and tasty enough without it, and 5) mixed in 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon with the dry ingredients. Would definitely make this again!
I devoured 2 slices and needed to resist going for piece number 3.
Not sweet enough. Made into one loaf and cooked for extra time. Still came out under-cooked. Not tasty at all.
substitute 1c Milk for 1C greek yogurt and eliminate the lemon juice. Bred has a bit more body and is airy.

This is the second year I’ve used this recipe during rhubarb season. I love it. My neighbor swears she doesn’t like rhubarb, but she loves this bread. She always wants more after I share a loaf with her. I use pecans instead of walnuts.
Very disappointing. Flavors of sugar and walnuts came through but rhubarb was barely detectable.
Wish I had read the comments and put into 3 loaf pans instead of the 2 the recipe called for.
Not going to make again. It's not a bread and not a cake. Flavor not there. Uses to many dishes.
Sent this recipe to my sister. It’s delicious! Not too sweet.
